## Analytic interfaces

<!-- passage:sec-analytic-interfaces -->

Abstract fields, forms, norms and error data that the later representations must supply.

### Abstract steady certificate data (L15)

`Breakdown.SteadyCert.FracCertData`. This record supplies the abstract profile, multiplier, row and adjoint data used by reusable cell estimates. Its spatial profiles and rotation rate belong to the steady interface; the active Appendix B certificate later uses time-periodic CellLayerData.

Paper: No separate numbered paper counterpart; general steady-certificate interface reused by the cell analysis. Source: [lines 15–61](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L15-L61). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCert/Defs.lean#L117-L163).

### Orientation of three components (L86)

`Breakdown.CellCert.permSign`. The alternating sign fixes the curl convention in cylindrical component arrays. Repeated indices contribute zero; the order of the two gradient indices matters.

Paper: Appendix B.3, (B.25), p.57; component implementation of curl G. Source: [lines 86–89](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L86-L89). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/StatementDefs.lean#L25-L28).

### Abstract cell approximation data (L91)

`Breakdown.CellCert.FracCellData`. This extends the steady-certificate record with a region, polynomial-model fields, approximation losses and spectral bounds. The fields are inputs; validity and error inequalities are supplied by separate predicates.

Paper: No separate numbered paper counterpart; abstract local estimates supporting Appendix B.3. Source: [lines 91–123](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L91-L123). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/StatementDefs.lean#L48-L80).

### Constraint matrix field (L1904)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinField`. Turns the stored polynomial constraint coefficients into the period-one matrix field Ξᵢ. The action on a perturbation is defined elsewhere.

Paper: Appendix B.1, (B.10), p.52. Source: [lines 1904–1905](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1904-L1905). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1100-L1101).

### Mode density on the quarter-plane (L1915)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDensity`. Evaluates the full mode form using the parameter's period, weights and bounds at time zero and angle zero. It is the reduced Iι density, before multiplication by r.

Paper: Appendix B.2, (B.16)–(B.18), pp.54–55; Appendix B.3, (B.23), pp.56–57. Source: [lines 1915–1918](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1915-L1918). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1111-L1114).

### Mean positive stretching part (L1920)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.stretchPosMean`. Averages the positive part of the stretching expression over time and angle. Taking the positive part before averaging differs from taking the positive part of the averaged expression.

Paper: Appendix B.2, (B.16)–(B.18), pp.54–55; Appendix B.3, (B.23), pp.56–57. Source: [lines 1920–1922](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1920-L1922). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1116-L1118).

**Checker care.**

- **positive-part-and-infinity**: Keep the positive-part operation inside the time/angle average and retain the extended-real finiteness distinction. Replacing mean(max(J,0)) by max(mean(J),0), or treating infinity as a finite numeric accumulator, changes the hypothesis.

### Positive reduced form integral (L1924)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.formPos`. Adds the sum of positive mode-density integrals and the mean positive stretching integral, with cylindrical weight r. Its value lies in the extended nonnegative reals and can be infinite.

Paper: Appendix B.2, (B.16)–(B.18), pp.54–55; Appendix B.3, (B.23), pp.56–57. Source: [lines 1924–1927](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1924-L1927). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1120-L1123).

**Checker care.**

- **positive-part-and-infinity**: Keep the positive-part operation inside the time/angle average and retain the extended-real finiteness distinction. Replacing mean(max(J,0)) by max(mean(J),0), or treating infinity as a finite numeric accumulator, changes the hypothesis.

### Two required symmetry generators (L1971)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsModeClass`. Requires positive azimuthal order and membership of the half-time rotation and spatial flip in Γ. This predicate alone does not say that every element of Γ is generated by them.

|---|---|
| The symmetry order satisfies κ≥1. | The azimuthal order is at least one. |

**Checker care.**

- **two-harmonic-coordinate-systems**: Distinguish lattice labels (ι₁,ι₂) from frequency pairs (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). Their flip operations differ, and κ>0 is needed for injectivity of the frequency map.

### Coefficient for the adjoint norm (L3738)

`Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff`. The L³ route contributes 2/(√3 w_*), and the L² route contributes c_w/√w_*, before multiplication by n_ψ.

- **norm-route-choice**: Keep the Boolean choice of L³ or L² norm aligned with its numerical coefficient. The cubed operator/field norm integral and the squared norm integral cannot be interchanged or estimated using a differently normalised matrix norm without a proved bound.

### Polynomial in cell coordinates (L1744)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly`. Stores a square complex coefficient array through one degree in each variable. Evaluation uses affine reference coordinates, rather than raw powers of r and z.

**Checker care.**

- **reference-polynomial-basis**: The coefficient array is evaluated in refR and refZ, each centred and scaled by the cell endpoints. Raw (r,z) coefficients require an exact basis conversion before they can denote the same polynomial.

**Checker care.**

- **model-support-must-be-bound**: The labels select the field sum while coefficient functions exist at all labels. Preserve the separate off-label and active-model conditions; omitting an active model label cannot be justified by merely shrinking a finite list.
- **model-error-decomposition**: Interpret each base model error as the remainder after both high and long pieces are subtracted. The high-piece bounds are separate, and curl-gradient remainder control is almost everywhere; replacing this decomposition by a single uniform model error changes the obligations.

**Checker care.**

The high-piece bounds are separate, and curl-gradient remainder control is almost everywhere; replacing this decomposition by a single uniform model error changes the obligations.

## Mesh and cells

<!-- passage:sec-mesh-and-cells -->

Cell geometry, weights, mode sets, spatial support and the mesh complement.

### Cylindrical radius (L213)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylRadius`. Returns r from the first two Cartesian coordinates, leaving the height coordinate out of the norm.

Paper: Appendix B.1, pp.50 and 52–53; cylindrical geometry of cells. Source: [lines 213–213](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L213). ### Cylindrical height (L215)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylHeight`. Returns the signed height z; reflection to the stored upper half-plane is performed separately.

Paper: Appendix B.1, pp.50 and 52–53; cylindrical geometry of cells. Source: [lines 215–215](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L215). ### Point in cylindrical coordinates (L217)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylPoint`. Builds the Cartesian point with radius r, angle θ and height z. Here θ is the spatial angle, whereas the paper uses θ for time and φ for angle.

Paper: Appendix B.1, pp.50 and 52–53; cylindrical geometry of cells. Source: [lines 217–218](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L217-L218). ### Radial frame vector (L220)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialUnit`. The first vector of the moving cylindrical frame is represented in the fixed Cartesian basis.

Paper: Appendix B.1, pp.50 and 52–53; cylindrical geometry of cells. Source: [lines 220–220](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L220). ### Angular frame vector (L222)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.angularUnit`. The second frame vector differentiates the radial direction with respect to angle and is orthogonal to it.

Paper: Appendix B.1, pp.50 and 52–53; cylindrical geometry of cells. Source: [lines 222–222](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L222). ### Axial frame vector (L224)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.axialUnit`. The third frame vector is the constant unit vector in the height direction.

Paper: Appendix B.1, pp.50 and 52–53; cylindrical geometry of cells. Source: [lines 224–224](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L224). `Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.azimuth`. Multiplies an integer mode by the azimuthal order. This one-frequency helper is distinct from the active two-integer label map of (B.2).

### Cell meeting the axis (L238)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.IsAxis`. An axis cell is recognised by the exact equality r₁=0, rather than a numerical tolerance.

- **exact-axis-branch**: Preserve the exact test r₁=0. Replacing it with a floating tolerance can switch the measure, polynomial family or boundary identities used by the proposition.

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.rect`. The stored meridian rectangle includes all four sides. Later integration permits shared boundaries of measure zero.

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.lineWeight`. Axis cells use radial weight r, whereas off-axis cells use weight one. This is the Jacobi versus Legendre distinction in (B.27).

Source: [lines 246–246](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L246). ### Reference radial coordinate (L248)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.refR`. Maps the radial interval affinely to the reference interval from minus one to one. A valid cell supplies the nonzero denominator.

Paper: Appendix B.1, p.52; Appendix B.3, (B.27), p.58. **Checker care.**

- **cell-width-denominators**: Bind each formula to a valid cell before using its inverse width or height. Lean division is total and returns a value for a zero denominator; a numerical exception is a different semantics.

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.refZ`. Maps the height interval affinely to the same reference interval; its orientation follows the ordered cell endpoints.

`Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh`. Checks nondegenerate cells, negligible overlaps, harmonic-set relations and basic degree bounds. Its skeleton lower bound is −1; the full layout condition later strengthens that to at least one on resolved modes.

- **mesh-validity-is-not-full-condition**: Base mesh validity permits an empty mesh and skeleton degree −1; the full certificate adds support, layout and nontrivial-profile obligations. ### Open meridian quarter-plane (L1909)

`Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane`. The analytic integrals use r>0 and z>0. The finite rectangles include their boundaries, whose contribution is handled by measure-zero statements.

### Region of a credit rectangle (L4269)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.region`. The patch uses the radial interval from inner to outer and the height interval from zero to height, adjacent to the reflection plane.

### Points belonging to one cell only (L4402)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownSolid`. The set keeps points in the chosen solid with r>0 and excludes points belonging to any other cell, removing shared faces from these pointwise split bounds.

Paper: Appendix B.3, pp.57, 59–60, polynomial models and the description of Proposition B.4; the explicit high/long split is an additional formal encoding. Source: [lines 4402–4403](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4402-L4403). **Checker care.**

- **owned-cell-and-common-null-set**: The split bounds use uniquely owned cell portions with r>0; exterior faces can remain when they are not shared. IsSplitPartAE requires one planar null set outside which the residual bound holds for all times and angles, which is stronger than independently choosing a null set for each time/angle.

### Pressure faces and test moments (L4544)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPressureSegmentation`. The segmentation covers every non-axis boundary side with disjoint interiors, correct opposite-side coordinates and orthonormal trace tests. Each conjunction remains an independent obligation.

Paper: Appendix B.1, p.53, polynomial test fields and (B.11); Appendix B.3, pp.57–60, local rows in (B.26). **Checker care.**

- **pressure-segmentation-scope**: Keep pressure segmentation as an independently required conjunct and check every covered side, disjointness clause, opposite-side value and trace orthogonality rule. The later radial-level condition does not make the entire segmentation optional on non-radial sides.

### Matching traces on the symmetry plane (L4646)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPlaneMatched`. Every side and pressure-side segment at z=0 must find an identical segment and test-coefficient function in the reflected layout. The displayed predicate is directional.

Paper: Appendix B.3, pp.57–60, resolved-mode data and local comparison (B.26). Source: [lines 4646–4652](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4646-L4652). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L3842-L3848).

**Checker care.**

- **plane-matching-direction**: IsPlaneMatched is a directional existence condition with exact equality of endpoints and test-coefficient functions. Use the parent quantifiers over reflected resolved labels, or check the desired direction explicitly; do not replace it by approximate geometric overlap.

### Forcing support lies in the cells (L4832)

`Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSupportFacts`. Binds each forcing field bᵢ to its compact shape data and asks the cells to cover a square containing its support. The support radius H is an existential real, with no sign condition in this structure.

| [`rc`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1181) | Positive radius parameter for the field's core construction. |

**Checker care.**

- **unused-jet-coefficients**: The evaluated spline uses finite active coordinates, but several symmetry/origin predicates quantify over all radial JetDof coordinates or all pairs. Define the omitted coefficient continuation and prove those identities there; checking only stored coefficients is insufficient without that argument.
- **symmetry-orbit-representatives**: Before completing symmetry orbits, check one representative per orbit and the fixed-orbit real/parity constraints. closureAmp has an explicit precedence order; silently merging conflicting representatives changes the decoded field.

**Checker care.**

- **active-knot-order**: Verify exact endpoints and strict ordering before using positive interval widths. The active index bounds make the getD defaults in joining tests unreachable, but the generic interpolation constructors do not enforce these guards themselves.

**Checker care.**

- **scaled-jet-zero-scales**: A zero node scale is allowed by HasSymmetricScale: Lean has 0⁻¹=0, so positive-order node jets can vanish in conversion while order zero remains unchanged. Decode this literally, or prove an additional nonzero-scale invariant before using an invertible-basis interpretation; this local degeneracy is not a witness to the full cell condition.
- **scaled-jet-list-defaults**: Use scale.getD k 1, bubbleConst.getD j 0 and breakpoint defaults 0 exactly. Missing bubble constants therefore remove those basis contributions, while missing node scales default to one; a uniform zero-fill rule changes the decoded field.

## Harmonics and symmetry

<!-- passage:sec-harmonics-and-symmetry -->

Temporal and azimuthal labels, orbit representatives, conjugation and reflection.

### Temporal harmonic integer (L1709)

`Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime`. Maps the lattice label ι to 2ι₂−ι₁, the integer multiplying 2π times the period-one time variable in (B.2).

Paper: Appendix B.1, (B.1)–(B.2), p.50; Appendix B.2, (B.12), p.53. Source: [lines 1709–1709](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1709). **Checker care.**

- **two-harmonic-coordinate-systems**: Distinguish lattice labels (ι₁,ι₂) from frequency pairs (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). Their flip operations differ, and κ>0 is needed for injectivity of the frequency map.

### Azimuthal harmonic integer (L1711)

`Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth`. Maps ι to κι₁, the integer multiplying the spatial angle in (B.2).

### Labels within the long cutoff (L4454)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellModelLong.IsLowLabel`. The test uses only |ι₁|≤cut, so it is an azimuthal label cutoff and does not bound the temporal index ι₂.

Paper: Appendix B.3, pp.57, 59–60, polynomial models and the description of Proposition B.4; the explicit high/long split is an additional formal encoding. Source: [lines 4454–4454](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4454). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L3650).

**Checker care.**

- **high-and-long-cancellation**: Polynomial moment cancellation uses ordinary dr dz, covers every temporal/angular label, and reaches bidegree 2·deg+1 in the active split. Long-mode cancellation excludes |ι₁|≤2·cut with no bound on ι₂; neither condition follows from a few discrete samples.

## Shape bounds

Chart bounds, model fields, weak Hessians and uniform parameter dependence.

### Upper-half step coefficient (L2402)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.upperValue`. The upper table is selected at the compactified radius σ and the signed height ratio η; the radial decay factor is applied by eval.

Paper: Appendix B.2, pp.53–54, scalar weights and auxiliary step functions before (B.14). Source: [lines 2402–2404](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L2402-L2404). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1598-L1600).

**Checker care.**

- **cell-index-endpoints**: Use the exact cellIndex rule: count internal knots b with b≤u. An internal knot belongs to the cell to its right, while the endpoint 1 selects the final active cell; do not substitute an extrapolation or half-open convention without proving agreement.

### Lower-half step coefficient (L2406)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.lowerValue`. The lower table uses −η, so both half-space tables are indexed by a nonnegative height coordinate.

### Step weight in physical space (L2410)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.eval`. The decoded weight is the selected table value times (1−σ) to an integer exponent; points on y₃=0 select the upper table.

Paper: Appendix B.2, pp.53–54, scalar weights and auxiliary step functions before (B.14). Source: [lines 2410–2412](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L2410-L2412). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1606-L1608).

**Checker care.**

- **cell-index-endpoints**: Use the exact cellIndex rule: count internal knots b with b≤u. An internal knot belongs to the cell to its right, while the endpoint 1 selects the final active cell; do not substitute an extrapolation or half-open convention without proving agreement.
- **scalar-plane-and-origin**: Keep all three scalar conventions distinct: StepDatum.eval uses the upper half on y₃=0; planeMinEval uses the minimum of the two sides there; ChartBound.eval handles y=0 with originValue before the integer power of σ. Negative powers and exact boundary values cannot be replaced by nearby samples.

## Rows and pins

<!-- passage:sec-rows-and-pins -->

Polynomial generators, Gram normalisation, constraint fields and actuator pairings.

### One real polynomial row generator (L2280)

`Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.generator`. Places the selected test on its cell and original label and uses the reflection machinery to define negative-height values. The realPart flag chooses the real or imaginary component.

Paper: Appendix B.1, (B.11), p.53. Source: [lines 2280–2283](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L2280-L2283). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1475-L1479).

**Checker care.**

- **conjugate-row-accounting**: Represent one member of each nonzero ± label pair, with both real and imaginary rows for every test, and only the real row for the zero label. The imaginary generator uses −i before taking a real part; use the same convention in its Gram matrix.

### Row generator as a space-time field (L2285)

`Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.generatorField`. Evaluates the selected cellwise polynomial generator with the global azimuthal order and the cell boxes.

Paper: Appendix B.1, (B.11), p.53. Source: [lines 2285–2286](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L2285-L2286). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L1481-L1482).

**Checker care.**

- **conjugate-row-accounting**: Represent one member of each nonzero ± label pair, with both real and imaginary rows for every test, and only the real row for the zero label. The imaginary generator uses −i before taking a real part; use the same convention in its Gram matrix.

### Gram matrix of real row generators (L2291)

`Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.fieldPairingMatrix`. Uses the full period-space pairing of the real generators. This matrix includes the real/imaginary and reflection conventions of the generator construction.

Paper: Appendix B.1, (B.11), p.53. Source: [lines 2291–2292](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L2291-L2292). **Checker care.**

- **inverse-square-root-branch**: The row mixing uses a Hermitian functional-calculus inverse square root and has a zero fallback otherwise. Bind it to the positive-definite block-Gram construction and the exact global real generator matrix.

### Inverse square root of the row Gram (L2295)

`Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.mix`. Uses the functional calculus inverse square root when the Gram matrix is Hermitian, and zero otherwise. The positive-definiteness proof supplies the intended orthogonalisation behaviour.

Paper: Appendix B.1, (B.11), p.53. `Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowFieldOf`. Mixes the real generators by the inverse-square-root matrix. The paper's row weight is stored separately in rowWeightOf, so this field alone does not include its square-root weight.

- **row-weight-scale**: Keep the orthonormal row fields separate from testWeight/coercivity. Prove coercivity>0 and the squared row-bound inequality; copying the paper's weighted rows into both places would apply the weight twice.

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond`. Requires radial and polar node or bubble coefficients beyond the chosen support radius to vanish, with quantifiers over all natural indices. Missing breakpoints are read as the support radius itself.

## Potentials

<!-- passage:sec-potentials -->

Adjoint potential representations, residual decompositions and dual estimates.

### Spatial second derivative (L3515)

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.secondDeriv`. The Hessian is an iterated Fréchet derivative, whose trace supplies the Laplacian in the residual formula.

Paper: No separate numbered paper counterpart; differential operator used in Appendix B.4, (B.51)–(B.52). Source: [lines 3515–3516](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3515-L3516). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L2711-L2712).

### Divergence of a linear-map field (L3518)

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.matrixDivergence`. The contraction differentiates K along each coordinate vector and then applies the resulting linear map to that same vector. Compare this convention before matching the paper's div Fᵀ notation.

Paper: Appendix B.4, (B.51)–(B.56), pp.67–68, and Lemma B.12. Source: [lines 3518–3519](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3518-L3519). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L2714-L2715).

**Checker care.**

- **adjoint-matrix-conventions**: Match matrix action, transpose and divergence conventions before comparing (B.52). In pinFlux the antisymmetric generator derivative is intentional; replacing it by a bare Laplacian without the divergence-free identity can introduce a wrong sign or transpose.

### Transpose action on a vector (L3521)

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.transposeApply`. The component formula computes Kᵀz for a real linear map K, as required by the adjoint transport term.

Paper: Appendix B.4, (B.51)–(B.56), pp.67–68, and Lemma B.12. Source: [lines 3521–3522](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3521-L3522). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L2717-L2718).

**Checker care.**

- **adjoint-matrix-conventions**: Match matrix action, transpose and divergence conventions before comparing (B.52). In pinFlux the antisymmetric generator derivative is intentional; replacing it by a bare Laplacian without the divergence-free identity can introduce a wrong sign or transpose.

### Derivative in normalized time (L3524)

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.timeDerivative`. The derivative is in the period-one variable θ; the reciprocal physical period is supplied separately by adjointTransport.

Paper: Appendix B.4, (B.51)–(B.56), pp.67–68, and Lemma B.12. Source: [lines 3524–3525](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3524-L3525). ### Adjoint advection difference (L3527)

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.advectionShift`. The expression (∇δ)ᵀζ−(δ·∇)ζ is the formal adjoint contribution of the linearized advection.

Paper: Appendix B.4, (B.51)–(B.56), pp.67–68, and Lemma B.12. Source: [lines 3527–3528](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3527-L3528). **Checker care.**

- **adjoint-matrix-conventions**: Match matrix action, transpose and divergence conventions before comparing (B.52). In pinFlux the antisymmetric generator derivative is intentional; replacing it by a bare Laplacian without the divergence-free identity can introduce a wrong sign or transpose.

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointTransport`. The time term uses −1/P, and the dilation adjoint contributes −ζ−(y·∇)ζ/2 before the advection difference.

### Azimuthal dual bound (L3576)

`Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded`. The expansion has distinct (component,time-frequency,azimuthal-order) triples, measurable amplitudes and an almost-everywhere spatial identity at every time. Its squared weight is (|m|+1/2)⁻² with circular-component weights.

Paper: Appendix B.4, dual-bound definition and Lemma B.11, pp.65–66; (B.50). Source: [lines 3576–3585](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3576-L3585). **Checker care.**

- **azimuthal-distinct-channels**: Check injectivity of the full (component,frequency,order) triple. If a raw expansion contains repeats, sum their complex amplitudes before computing the bound; do not add their squared norms separately. Use weights 1/2,1/2,1, the factor 2π in time and denominator (|order|+1/2)² exactly.
- **azimuthal-uniform-expansion**: The expansion holds for every time outside a spatial null set that may depend on that time, while amplitude rotation covariance is pointwise for every angle and point. Retain these distinct quantifier scopes and measurability obligations.

**Checker care.**

- **shared-dual-witnesses**: Use one decomposition R=R₁+R₂ with its two bounds for DualBounded, and one family δᵢ in free_dual that works for every α∈K. Choosing unrelated witnesses for separate descendant inequalities checks a different proposition.
- **empty-fitted-directions**: On the specialised cell route AdjointEntryLinks requires fittedSet=∅ for each active adjoint. The fitted norms then contribute nothing, but all complementary weighted free-direction and period-rate obligations remain.
- **ellipsoid-coordinate-scales**: The radius formula for an ellipsoid coordinate divides by |scaleᵢ|. Preserve the nonzero-scale conditions on the active certificate route and the distinction between box coordinates in J and complementary ellipsoid coordinates.

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotScalar`. A tensor-product Hermite amplitude is multiplied by explicit near-origin, far-field and axis factors. Endpoint vanishing may supply part of the required radial order.

### Polar sine from the height ratio (L6741)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.polarSine`. Computes √(1−η²) using the height ratio defined on Cartesian points. Its values at the origin and axis follow the existing totalized chart conventions.

Paper: Appendix B.4, fields G_j,U_j,F_j,q_j preceding (B.51), p.67; the coefficient format is explicitly omitted in the paper. Source: [lines 6741–6741](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6741). ### Decode a scalar potential mode (L6743)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.scalarValue`. Combines time, azimuthal and radial phases with radial weights, axis factors and the spline value. The optional polar sine is separate from the integer axis power.

Source: [lines 6743–6749](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6743-L6749). - **potential-phase-convention**: Preserve the integer time label, shifted azimuthal frequency and phaseIndex multiplier separately; they are different inputs to the complex exponential.

### Decode one vector component (L6751)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.componentValue`. Supplies the component-specific azimuthal shift and polar-sine choice to the scalar potential decoder.

### Recover Cartesian components (L6755)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.coordsOfComponents`. Recovers x and y from x+iy and x−iy using factors 1/2 and 1/(2i), while leaving the axial component unchanged.

Paper: Appendix B.4, fields G_j,U_j,F_j,q_j preceding (B.51), p.67; the coefficient format is explicitly omitted in the paper. - **complex-component-factors**: The half factors in the horizontal reconstruction are essential. Do not treat plus/minus amplitudes as independent Cartesian coordinates.

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.vectorPotential`. Sums the selected complex components, reconstructs Cartesian coordinates and takes the real vector. The selector chooses the G or U amplitude family.

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxVector`. Forms a vector in the input index by combining the radial direction with the polar vector, for one output component and harmonic key.

### One entry of the potential flux (L6779)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxEntry`. Sums the flux modes, reconstructs the output component and takes its real part. The two indices are output component a and input direction i.

### Flux as a continuous linear map (L6783)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxMap`. Turns the output-by-input matrix into a continuous linear map. Relative to the paper’s derivative convention this represents the transposed flux used in div F_jᵀ.

Source: [lines 6783–6784](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6783-L6784). **Checker care.**

- **flux-matrix-convention**: Keep the output-row/input-column convention when matching the paper’s div F_jᵀ. Frobenius norms survive transpose, but divergence orientation does not.

### Decode the potential pressure (L6786)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.pressureValue`. Uses the unshifted harmonic azimuth, with no extra polar-sine factor, and takes the real part of the scalar sum.

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries.toPotentialData`. Packages the decoded G, U, flux and pressure functions into the adjoint-potential interface. This data conversion contains no proof of regularity.

### Ordered jet breakpoints only (L6792)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsJetMesh`. Requires strictly ordered breaks with specified endpoints. It intentionally omits the stronger joining conditions of IsJetAxis, allowing the tangential discontinuities permitted in the flux representation.

Paper: Appendix B.4, fields G_j,U_j,F_j,q_j preceding (B.51), p.67; the coefficient format is explicitly omitted in the paper. Source: [lines 6792–6795](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6792-L6795). | Direct field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [`sorted`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6793) | The breakpoint list is strictly increasing. |
| [`first`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6794) | The first breakpoint is exactly the stated lower endpoint. |
| [`last`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6795) | The last breakpoint is exactly the stated upper endpoint. |

**Checker care.**

- **jet-mesh-versus-jet-axis**: Do not replace IsJetMesh by IsJetAxis or assume it proves continuity. The flux conditions use the stronger predicate only in the direction needed for normal-flux continuity.

### Zero radial jets at the origin (L6797)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartVanishOrder`. Requires all node-jet coefficients below the requested order to vanish at the first radial breakpoint, for every polar degree of freedom.

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.EndVanishOrder`. Requires the low-order radial node coefficients to vanish at the final compactified breakpoint, with the final index computed by cellCount.

### Degree of freedom touches an end (L6803)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.dofMeetsEndCells`. Classifies node and bubble degrees of freedom that can affect the first or last cell. Natural subtraction in N−1 is truncated at zero.

### Amplitude vanishes in axis cells (L6807)

`Breakdown.PotentialShape.AxisCellsVanish`. Requires zero coefficients for every polar degree of freedom that touches either polar endpoint cell. This supplies an alternative to an explicit positive axis power.

## Local forms

<!-- passage:sec-local-forms -->

Finite cell coordinates, polynomial models and local quadratic inequalities.

### Real quadratic form (L141)

`Breakdown.CellCert.Finite.quadValue`. Evaluates the real matrix form on a real vector. Symmetry and positivity are separate requirements, so this evaluator alone supplies neither.

Paper: Appendix B.3, (B.38)–(B.42), pp.61–63; real quadratic-form convention. Source: [lines 141–141](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L141). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/StatementDefs.lean#L127).

### Curl from gradient components (L283)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlComp`. The component formula reads the gradient entry with output index first and derivative index second. That convention must be kept when comparing the paper's printed curl array.

### Polynomial basis coefficients (L298)

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBases`. Stores coefficient functions for every natural degree in r and z. A finite file therefore needs a specified continuation beyond the degrees it stores.

| [`heightCoef`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L300) | Coefficient of each monomial in every height basis polynomial. |

**Checker care.**

- **infinite-basis-continuation**: Supply the complete basis family, with the proved continuation beyond stored degrees. Uniform zero extension violates positive leading coefficients and orthonormality at every natural degree.

### Radial orthonormal polynomial (L306)

The radial polynomial is ∑ᵢ₌₀ʲ aⱼᵢrⁱ, so its degree is at most j. The separate positive-leading-coefficient condition makes the degree exactly j.

Source: [lines 306–306](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L306). - **infinite-basis-continuation**: Supply the complete basis family, with the proved continuation beyond stored degrees. Uniform zero extension violates positive leading coefficients and orthonormality at every natural degree.

The height polynomial is ∑ᵢ₌₀ˡ bₗᵢzⁱ. Orthonormality and the positive leading coefficient are separate requirements on the family.

### Pointwise three-part model split (L4405)

**Checker care.**

- **owned-cell-and-common-null-set**: The split bounds use uniquely owned cell portions with r>0; exterior faces can remain when they are not shared. IsSplitPartAE requires one planar null set outside which the residual bound holds for all times and angles, which is stronger than independently choosing a null set for each time/angle.

### High vector moments vanish (L4419)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsVecOrthogonal`. Every label and component has zero moments against all rectangular monomials with each degree at most the supplied bound; the integral here has no additional radial weight.

**Checker care.**

- **high-and-long-cancellation**: Polynomial moment cancellation uses ordinary dr dz, covers every temporal/angular label, and reaches bidegree 2·deg+1 in the active split. Long-mode cancellation excludes |ι₁|≤2·cut with no bound on ι₂; neither condition follows from a few discrete samples.

### Full polynomial model decomposition (L4456)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellModelSplit`. Each of the four fields is split into model, high, long and residual parts. Orthogonality, angular gaps, symmetry, measurability and nonnegative error budgets are separate obligations.

|---|---|

| [`vorticity`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4461-L4462) | Pointwise decomposition of vorticity on the same solid. |
| [`strain`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4463-L4464) | Pointwise decomposition of strain on the same solid. |

| [`long_modes`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4467-L4469) | All four long pieces have zero modes whenever \|ι₁\|≤2·cut, for every temporal label. |

**Checker care.**

- **owned-cell-and-common-null-set**: The split bounds use uniquely owned cell portions with r>0; exterior faces can remain when they are not shared. IsSplitPartAE requires one planar null set outside which the residual bound holds for all times and angles, which is stronger than independently choosing a null set for each time/angle.
- **high-and-long-cancellation**: Polynomial moment cancellation uses ordinary dr dz, covers every temporal/angular label, and reaches bidegree 2·deg+1 in the active split. Long-mode cancellation excludes |ι₁|≤2·cut with no bound on ι₂; neither condition follows from a few discrete samples.

### Angular derivative in a moving frame (L4494)

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.turnVector`. The operator ikx plus the frame-rotation correction mixes the radial and angular components, while the vertical component has only ikx₃.

Paper: Appendix B.1, p.53, polynomial test fields and (B.11); Appendix B.3, pp.57–60, local rows in (B.26). Source: [lines 4494–4495](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L4494-L4495). **Checker care.**

- **cylindrical-angular-test-derivative**: Use the moving-frame angular derivative ikx+e_z×x and its division by r, including the component mixing. The solenoidal and axis-regularity conditions must hold on the whole rectangle; the generic formula alone does not certify smoothness at r=0.

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowSlotForm`. The local matrix is integrated against tensor-basis slot pairs and pulled back by the slot rows; different angular slots have zero cross coefficient here.

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowStrainOf`. Each gradient component uses tensor polynomial coefficients through degree Q in both variables, indexed by the mode's tagged lowStrain coordinates.

**Checker care.**

- **parent-map-not-acyclicity**: The data type contains an arbitrary finite parent map. Later conditions require a unique parentless root, but do not literally require acyclicity; the proof uses finite summed cancellation. An acyclic file format is a stronger representation choice, not a missing extracted field.

**Checker care.**

- **signed-factorisation-conventions**: Use the exact signs of the positive and negative column products, the two error matrices and the nonpivot radius subtraction. Complex forms require conjugate transposes and complex moduli, not real transposes and entrywise real parts.
- **two-real-columns-per-complex-column**: Each negative complex column produces two indexed real columns, with an injective map into the global column type. Count the indices even when some resulting vectors vanish or coincide, and preserve the square-root factor.
- **zero-complex-node-factor**: The factor is allowed to be zero. Together with positive pivot slack and slack_le this permits no real pivots at that node; it does not by itself invalidate a node with an empty pivot set. This is a source-level algebraic consequence, not a new Lean replay.

### Global negative multiplier form (L5022)

`Breakdown.CertCell.globalForm`. The global upper bound is the negative β-square with coercivity and global error, plus the negative ζ-square. Substituting 3/50 and 1000 recovers the constants of (B.43).

Paper: Appendix B.3, (B.43), p.63. Source: [lines 5022–5024](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5022-L5024). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L4218-L4220).

### Carry a complex form to real data (L5026)

`Breakdown.CertCell.realLeafForm`. Computes the real matrix of the pulled-back complex form using the conjugate transpose of P. Its argument coordinates are real global unknowns.

Paper: Appendix B.3, (B.38), pp.61–62. Source: [lines 5026–5028](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5026-L5028). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L4222-L4224).

**Checker care.**

- **conjugate-pullback**: Use Re(P* Ψ P), with complex conjugation in the adjoint. A transpose-only or lower-triangle substitution changes the form.

### Segment for a skeleton key (L5067)

`Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg`. Builds the segment used to interpret a common boundary key. Its unused opposite level is chosen as lev+1, so this helper must not be confused with a cell’s physical width.

Paper: Appendix B.3, pp.57–60: relations between cell and global unknowns; no separate paper counterpart for this representation helper. Source: [lines 5067–5067](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5067). ### A row read from a common key (L6341)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.KeyRow`. Excludes private keys, checks the symmetry evaluation and both optional components, then requires exact equality with the resulting complex row vector.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. ### Subsegment used by a split row (L6349)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileSeg`. Constructs the segment for one tile of a face-moment subdivision using its local interval and test coefficients.

### Flux reconstruction on a subsegment (L6352)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileFlux`. Uses stream endpoint differences to reconstruct the constant normal-velocity moment. The radial branch divides by the face radius; the horizontal branch divides by the leading linear test coefficient.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6352–6360](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6352-L6360). **Checker care.**

- **split-flux-denominators**: The raw formula permits zero denominators through Lean’s totalized division. SplitRow requires the appropriate denominator to be nonzero when that flux branch is used.

### Choose direct or flux reconstruction (L6362)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.tileVec`. Uses the stream-flux formula only for a tile marked flux and degree zero. All other local moments use their optional direct real and imaginary slots.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6362–6363](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6362-L6363). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L5558-L5559).

### Check a subdivided moment row (L6365)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.SplitRow`. Requires a nonempty contiguous tiling, exact test-polynomial identities, valid shared coordinates and justified flux substitutions. The resulting row equality is exact, with every listed coefficient included.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6365–6400](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6365-L6400). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L5561-L5596).

**Checker care.**

- **subdivision-cover-and-identities**: Check strict tile widths, adjacent endpoints, both outer endpoints and polynomial identities for every real argument. A pointwise quadrature check does not prove SplitRow.
- **split-deleted-key-exclusion**: A split row may not use a gauge-deleted parent or any nonzero-coefficient gauge-deleted child key.

### Check a stream-flux row (L6402)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.FluxRow`. Provides separate radial and horizontal moment identities. The horizontal branch also requires the linear velocity moment to have smaller rank and to be used.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6402–6421](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6402-L6421). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L5598-L5617).

**Checker care.**

- **flux-rank-and-denominators**: Retain the radial positive-radius test, the horizontal nonzero leading coefficient and the smaller-rank dependency; the reconstruction formula alone is insufficient.

### Combine local linear relations (L6423)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.relCoef`. Forms the coefficient of one datum in a finite linear combination of the layout’s relation rows.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6423–6426](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6423-L6426). ### Solve a relation for one row (L6429)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.DerivedRow`. The chosen combination has coefficient one on the target and zero on pressure data. Every other nonzero coefficient uses a non-unused row of smaller rank, giving a well-founded reconstruction.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6429–6435](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6429-L6435). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L5624-L5631).

**Checker care.**

- **derived-row-acyclic**: Check the exact unit target coefficient, pressure cancellation and every strict rank decrease. Permitting a self-dependent cycle would change the justification.

### A row evaluated directly from a cell (L6437)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.LeafRow`. Binds the real component to a cell datum and allows an optional imaginary component. Omitting the imaginary component is permitted only at harmonic zero.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6437–6445](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6437-L6445). ### Coordinate invisible to the forms (L6447)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.UnusedRow`. Requires the sparse row itself, the entire row and column of the cell matrix, and every credit use to vanish. The coordinate remains free in InRowRange.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. Source: [lines 6447–6451](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6447-L6451). **Checker care.**

- **unused-does-not-mean-zero**: Do not set an unused coordinate to zero when checking local inequalities. Its cell form and credit effects vanish, but InRowRange still permits an arbitrary complex value.

### Velocity-moment row with cutoff (L6454)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.velRow`. Reads the requested side-velocity row when its natural degree fits the layout and returns zero beyond that range.

Paper: Appendix B.3, p.57 and the coordinate discussion on p.60; the exact skeleton-row representation is not written in the paper. ### A velocity-moment row is ready (L6458)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.velReady`. Requires a valid in-range degree, a strictly smaller rank than the target, and a justification other than unused.

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cornerRow`. An absent corner returns the zero row. A present corner uses the corresponding cell velocity datum.

### Reconstruct a normal derivative row (L6475)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.NormalRow`. Uses the face divergence relation, polynomial test derivatives and endpoint velocities to determine a normal gradient moment. An absent lower corner is permitted only on a horizontal segment starting at the axis.

- **normal-row-polynomial-identity**: The test derivative expansion must hold for every real argument, with radial factors and boundary signs preserved. Every velocity and corner row used must be ready.

### Validate the chosen row reason (L6518)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Accounted`. Dispatches on the seven row-reason constructors and asks for that constructor’s exact justification. This is the complete row-level obligation, rather than a tag-only test.

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowConditions`. Links the stored X_Q to the row construction, supplies the A₀ upper bound (B.43), and makes pressure heads invisible. The field named global_eq is a one-sided inequality.

## Assembly

<!-- passage:sec-assembly -->

Local-to-global row maps, potential and pairing forms, charges and elimination.

### All coordinates of one cell (L5320)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellVars`. Includes the resolved cell data, auxiliary ports, β coordinates and ζ coordinates. The type is larger than the polynomial velocity coefficients alone.

Paper: Appendix B.3, cell unknowns and global unknowns, p.57. Source: [lines 5320–5321](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5320-L5321). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L4516-L4517).

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChargeBound`. The paper’s s₁,s₂,s₃,h are represented as curl, product, gradient and length charges. The length is required to be positive and independent of the harmonic label on the region.

Paper: Appendix B.3, (B.25), p.57. Source: [lines 5323–5334](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5323-L5334). | [`band_slack`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5492) | The elimination slack lies in [0,1). |

**Checker care.**

- **full-row-domain**: Check residual_value_le on every InRowRange vector, including its free unused, port, gauge and pressure-head directions; checking only the image of X_Q is insufficient.
- **slack-zero-exactness**: slack_zero quantifies every point p, without restricting p to the cell. Do not silently weaken it to cell interiors or almost-everywhere equality.

### Gram matrix of tested row fields (L5540)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowGram`. Rows from different harmonic labels have zero pairing. Equal-label entries integrate one test times the conjugate of the other with radial weight r.

Paper: Appendix B.3, right-hand-side pairings in Proposition B.4, (B.33)–(B.34), pp.59–60; detailed row formulas are not written in the paper. Source: [lines 5540–5542](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L5540-L5542). **Checker care.**

- **row-gram-conjugation**: Use the declared i,i′ ordering and complex conjugation, together with the radial measure; a Euclidean coefficient dot product is a different Gram matrix.

**Checker care.**

- **potential-domain**: Prove the kept and port inequalities for all InRowRange vectors; retain its independent complex gauge, head, unused and port directions.
- **model-label-coverage-uses**: Both group_link and groups_cover depend on exact active modelLabels; rows_groups_cover adds a third use in RowFunctionalConditions. Covering a finite support superset is a sufficient alternative.
- **global-source-identity**: source_eq is an exact identity at every p, without a cell-membership premise. Polynomial coefficient identities are a suitable way to establish it.
- **projection-is-not-idempotence**: projection_block is a support condition only; do not add an unstated assumption that bandProjection is orthogonal or idempotent.

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingConditions`. Bounds B_Q on S and controls the nonzero pairing tails in both resolved and unresolved modes. The Gram inequalities quantify real β,ζ weights even though the matrices are complex.

**Checker care.**

- **pairing-zero-test**: gamma_resolved and gamma_other branch on nonzero almost-everywhere profiles. Omitting a profile requires exact a.e. vanishing, not small sampled values.
- **pairing-real-weights**: The Gram tests quantify real β,ζ vectors; preserve that domain and the factor 2 in pairWeightOf when reducing to a real matrix inequality.

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longSourceCost`. For a low source label uses the high cost, and for a high source label uses both low and high costs. This differs from longRowCost.

### Reciprocal long-range row charge (L5998)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longRowTerm`. Returns zero only when both long-range velocity and vorticity errors vanish exactly; otherwise it returns the reciprocal row cost.

**Checker care.**

- **natural-index-extension**: actuatorModel is indexed by ℕ and actuator_model_regular checks every natural index. A decoder that stores only k models must specify and validate a continuation, such as a justified zero extension.
- **third-active-label-use**: rows_groups_cover is the third active-model coverage obligation, in addition to group_link and groups_cover.
- **uniform-reciprocal-period**: period_box is uniform over the full box/ellipsoid parameter domain; samples do not establish this bound.

### Allowed vectors for local inequalities (L6547)

`Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange`. Only used cell coordinates must agree with one real row vector plus arbitrary complex gauge and pressure-head contributions. Unused cell coordinates and ports remain arbitrary complex values, while both β and ζ blocks must be real.

Paper: Appendix B.3, the domain x=X_Q x_g in (B.26), p.58; Lean uses this larger explicitly described domain. Source: [lines 6547–6553](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6547-L6553). Implementation: [the matching occurrence](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StatementDefs.lean#L5742-L5749).

**Checker care.**

- **row-range-free-directions**: Form the full real generator space, including unused and port real/imaginary unit vectors, complex gauge and head directions, and real β,ζ directions. Checking only rowEmbed’s image does not imply the three required local inequalities.

### Potential checks after regularity (L6639)

`Breakdown.CertCell.PotentialEntryConditions`. This is an implication: once eight analytic and geometric prerequisites are supplied, the potential conditions must follow. Those prerequisites are obtained elsewhere in the complete cell route.

Source: [lines 6639–6646](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L6639-L6646). **Checker care.**

- **implication-scope**: Preserve antecedents and their polarity when expanding obligations; this declaration is not an unconditional copy of PotentialConditions or an independent list of eight new numerical checks.

- **pressure-blind-two-sided**: pressure_blind requires zero rows and columns for several matrices plus zero source coefficients. Merely deleting pressure coordinates from one matrix check is insufficient.

## Exterior and omitted modes

Coverage and bounds for unresolved harmonics and unbounded regions.

### Trace-free stretching constant (L187)

`Breakdown.CellCert.Exterior.traceFreeConst`. This is the square root of seven halves appearing in the mixed gradient-velocity loss. It is the fixed constant before any larger exterior majorant is chosen.

`Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.SetPieceBounds`. One record can cover an infinite harmonic set when its class, signed piece membership, frequency bounds and coupling envelopes are uniform there.

| [`crossHigh_nonneg`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3491) | The cross ceiling f₀₁∞ is nonnegative. |
| [`test`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L3492) | The combined velocity and cross costs fit beneath f₁∞ as in (B.30). |

**Checker care.**

- **off-mode-positive-denominators**: The scalar formulas divide by r, the stretching length and auxiliary weights. Establish r>0 from the open quarter-plane, the length/step positivity from the associated conditions, and Λ₀>0 on the exterior branch before interval evaluation.
- **exterior-shared-witness-and-branch**: Keep the single shared radial function R and its global bounds throughout the radial-graph branch. The square-exterior alternative additionally requires every tested angular frequency to be zero; check the selected branch with its own Λ₀ bound.

- **strictness-and-finiteness**: Preserve strict transfer, contraction and nontriviality inequalities. The .toReal gradient integral must be read with the full positive-weight hypotheses; an infinite integral is not a large finite number.

**Checker care.**

- **conditional-certificate-boundary**: This is a premise about specific decoded data, not evidence that such data have been supplied. A checker acceptance must imply all fifteen fields for the same seven arguments.
